You are running the TEA workflow `bmad-testarch-nfr` against the project in `harbor-billing-ledger/`.

The workflow is in `skill/`. Read `skill/instructions.md` first, then execute every step file it
names in order, in full, without skipping or reordering. The step files are under `skill/steps-c/`.

----- run configuration -----
Resolve the workflow placeholders to these values:

- `{project-root}`: `harbor-billing-ledger`
- TEA config (`[core]` and `[modules.tea]`): `harbor-billing-ledger/_bmad/config.toml`
- `{test_artifacts}`: `harbor-billing-ledger/test-artifacts`
- `{skill-root}`: `skill`
- `{tea-knowledge}`: `bmod-tea/knowledge`
- `custom_nfr_categories`: ``

The NFR requirements and the thresholds for this service are stated under `harbor-billing-ledger/docs/`. The
evidence to audit them against is what you find under `harbor-billing-ledger/`. Discover both the way step-01
and step-03 say to; nothing outside that directory is evidence about this service.
The audit covers the whole service, so the `run_key` step-01 resolves is `system`.

----- what to produce -----
Write `harbor-billing-ledger/test-artifacts/nfr/nfr-assessment-system.md` from `skill/nfr-report-template.md`, carrying:

- one `## <Domain> Assessment` section for each of Performance, Security, Reliability, and
  Maintainability, in that order;
- inside each section, one finding per dimension the workflow evaluates, each stating its
  `**Status:**`, its `**Threshold:**`, its `**Actual:**`, and its `**Evidence:**`;
- an evidence citation that names the file it rests on, by a path under `harbor-billing-ledger/`;
- the `## Evidence Gaps` section the template declares; and
- the Gate YAML snippet the template ends with, carrying `overall_status` and the
  `audited_domains` block, one status per domain.

Do not add, edit, or delete any file under `harbor-billing-ledger/docs/`, `harbor-billing-ledger/evidence/`, or
`harbor-billing-ledger/config/`. This workflow audits evidence and generates none.

When you are done, print one line naming the file you wrote. Nothing else you print is read.
